argument.issue: Did the RPD err in finding an Internal Flight Alternative (IFA) in Mexico?

argument.weak_spot: The other side may argue the RPD's analysis was reasonable and based on available evidence.

argument.issue: Did the RPD improperly assess the burden of proof regarding the identity and reach of the agents of harm?
argument.claim: The RPD erred by imposing a heavy burden on the appellants to know all details about the agents of harm for IFA analysis.
argument.quote: The appellants submit that the RPD erred by imposing on the appellants the heavy burden of having to know all of the details about the agents of harm in order to determine whether there is an IFA.
argument.weak_spot: The other side may argue that some knowledge of the agents of harm is necessary for risk assessment.

best_match.label: same_question
best_match.issue: Is the RAD decision confirming the RPD finding that the Applicants are neither Convention refugees nor persons in need of protection reasonable?
best_match.quoted_paragraph: In short, I do not agree that the RAD’s Decision was unreasonable for any of the reasons raised by the Applicant. There is a clearly a discernable rational chain of analysis in the RAD’s findings that is, “justified in relation to the facts and law that constrain the decision maker” (Vavilov at para 85). I find the RAD undertook a thorough and rigorous independent assessment of the evidence, and further that the Decision is reasonable.

argument.issue: Would relocation to the proposed IFA be unreasonable or unduly harsh for the appellants?
argument.claim: Relocation would be unreasonable as the appellants lack support, have limited education and employment prospects, and would experience distress.
argument.quote: They do not have any family members or friends in the areas suggested so they will not have any support in relocating to those areas.
argument.weak_spot: The other side may argue that economic hardship and lack of support do not make relocation unreasonable under the law.
